answer: Graph Clique Anomaly Scoring. Agents submit interaction graphs post-hoc; a detector checks whether each identity's neighborhood forms a tight clique with abnormally uniform edge timing, flagging the cluster around any suspicious vertex. We also track the ratio of internal to external edges each identity touches, plus how often it acts as a bridge between otherwise disconnected groups. To survive, an attacker must build costly diverse organic history per fake identity, since one cheap marble of shared provenance sinks the whole ring.
